content:
I am very pleased to welcome Jesse and Guilherme to the CSLib Initiative.

@Jesse Alama has contributed to the JavaScript specification and worked in the Racket programming language before working primarily in Lean. He'll be keeping an eye on the CSLib CI work, in collaboration with the CI folks on the Mathlib side, polishing and expanding work on machine models (e.g., unlimited register machines) and equivalences (such as the equivalence of SKI calculus with untyped lambda calculus), as well as bridging CSLib to applied domains such as databases and query languages. More about Jesse: https://jessealama.net/

@Guilherme Lima will help with the ongoing port of AWS’s s2n-bignum from HOL Light to Lean 4. s2n-bignum is a collection of arithmetic routines written in machine code (64-bit x86 and ARM) and formally verified in HOL Light. The goal of the port is to produce a Lean 4 version of the library, adapted to Lean 4’s style of formalization and ecosystem, reusing any code and theories already provided by CSLib and, eventually, contributing new code and theories back to CSLib. The port code is available here. More about Guilherme: https://gflima.github.io/
